source: វិធានការចម្រុះគ្រប់គ្រងដំណាំ លើដំណាំស្រូវ (Integrated Pest Management on Rice), training slide deck, Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Battambang province, presented by Ms. Yem Sophy, Oct 20, 2017 (contact: ysophy168@gmail.com, 012 558 312)
text: Armyworm (Mythimna separata) has three related forms named in the deck: rice swarming caterpillar, common cutworm, and rice ear-cutting caterpillar. A single egg mass can hold roughly 500-1,000 eggs, and one female moth can lay eggs across roughly 8 sessions in her lifetime. The caterpillar damages rice by cutting through the stem/tiller at ground level, and damage is worse where nitrogen fertilizer is heavy and foliage is lush, since dense, soft growth favors egg-laying and larval feeding; the pest can spread rapidly within a field once numbers build up, and in dry fields it can also move onto rice from surrounding grasses. Natural egg parasitoids are noted as important in keeping this pest in check when not disrupted by unnecessary spraying.
